title: Robust Diamond Quantum Sensing in Double-Quantum 4-Ramsey Interferometry by Dual-Feedback Scheme
authors: Yuta Araki, Takeharu Sekiguchi, Yuji Hatano, Naota Sekiguchi, Zehan Li, Chikara Shinei, Masashi Miyakawa, Takashi Taniguchi, Tokuyuki Teraji, Hiroshi Abe, Shinobu Onoda, Takeshi Ohshima, Mutsuko Hatano, Takayuki Iwasaki
abstract: We developed a highly sensitive and long-term stable diamond quantum magnetometer by integrating a dual-feedback system that compensates for common- and differential-mode frequency shifts in double-quantum (DQ) 4-Ramsey interferometry. Detecting extremely weak magnetic-field signals requires extensive signal accumulation to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio. However, deviations from the optimal operating frequencies caused by thermal drift or environmental magnetic noise severely hinder the long-term stability of such a sensing system. To overcome the limitation, we first derived analytical solutions for the signal response to common- and differential-mode detunings based on a detuning-inclusive Hamiltonian to theoretically clarify the robustness limit in DQ 4-Ramsey sensing. Guided by this theoretical model, we introduced synchronized frequency modulation and a dual-feedback scheme to independently track and compensate for these frequency shifts while maintaining an optimal magnetic-field response. The proposed method enabled stable continuous operation against temperature variations of 2.8 K. By maintaining a magnetic field sensitivity of 7.0 pT/Hz^1/2 in the frequency range of 5-100 Hz for a prolonged duration of 4 hours, we achieved an extremely low noise floor of 64 fT/Hz^1/2. During prolonged continuous sensing, the system exhibited the expected 1/T^1/2 scaling with integration time T, and prevented both the underestimation of amplitude and waveform distortion. These results establish a robust approach for long-term DQ 4-Ramsey diamond magnetometry and demonstrate its potential for detecting weak biomagnetic signals.
summary: This paper presents a novel, robust method for diamond quantum magnetometry by integrating a dual-feedback control system into Double-Quantum 4-Ramsey interferometry. This scheme allows the sensor to independently track and compensate for common- and differential-mode frequency drifts caused by temperature or magnetic noise. The successful implementation enables long-term, stable measurements with extremely low noise floors, opening pathways for detecting weak biomagnetic signals.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving high magnetic field sensitivity and long-term stability in diamond quantum magnetometry while compensating for environmental drifts like thermal fluctuations.
main_result: The authors demonstrated stable continuous operation against 2.8 K temperature variations, achieving a magnetic field sensitivity of 7.0 pT/Hz^1/2 over 4 hours.
method: They developed and implemented a dual-feedback scheme using synchronized frequency modulation to independently track and compensate for common- and differential-mode frequency shifts.
model_or_system: The system utilizes Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond as quantum magnetometers, employing Double-Quantum (DQ) 4-Ramsey interferometry.

important_parameters: Temperature variation (2.8 K), integration time (4 hours), and the scaling of uncertainty ($\propto 1/\sqrt{T}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving analytical solutions for signal response using a detuning-inclusive Hamiltonian and assuming the applicability of the dual-feedback architecture.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level diagram and signal response for different detuning modes, while the setup diagrams detail the dual-feedback architecture and the complex microwave/RF mixing components used.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from theoretical derivation of signal response to detuning, introduces the limitations of standard sensing, proposes the dual-feedback scheme, and concludes with experimental validation showing stable, long-term operation.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it demonstrates advanced quantum control techniques (dual-feedback) to stabilize a solid-state quantum sensor against environmental noise, pushing the limits of measurement precision.

Fig. 3(a) illustrates the optical, MW, and RF experimental setup. A 532-nm laser beam was delivered through an optical fiber to the sensor head in a three-layer magnetic shield box. An optical power of 20–200 mW was focused onto the diamond using a convex lens with a focal length of 150 mm. The acousto-optic modulator (AOM) was stabilized by proportional-integral (PI) control implemented on a Red Pitaya Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) platform [28]. This feedback stabilization was used to suppress 1/𝑓intensity noise of the laser. Balanced detection was implemented following the method described in Ref. [14].
